summary: Iteration 11 — Home deck linear-timeline behaviour, single-batch cover prefetch, reader info-grid tight category icon, and discover-batch/category-media backend endpoints all verified. Pytest suite (6/6 passing) at /app/backend/tests/test_iter11_deck_batch.py covers discover-batch pagination/uniqueness/count-limits/interests, category-media?cutout=true&tight=true PNG RGBA, and /api/media hero WebP. Backend startup log confirms 'Media cache warm-up: 710 files'. Frontend at 390x844: first render shows exactly one deck-layer-next and NO deck-layer-previous; only ONE /api/discover-batch request (count=7) is fired, no /api/discover-next requests; the active hero is already complete (naturalWidth=896) before the deck is shown. Swipe-left introduces the previous layer, swipe-right returns to first card and removes it. After ~6 swipes-left, a second /api/discover-batch with exclude=<7 ids> is fired, deck grows to 14 with no duplicated ids and no abrupt jumps. Tapping a category tile resets the deck and issues a fresh batch with interests=, previous layer stays absent. Tapping the active card opens /deep-dive/. Reader info-grid on /deep-dive/black-holes-basics and /deep-dive/why-we-yawn: story-info-grid-category-icon src contains 'tight=true', loads (naturalWidth=273 for spazio, 143 for corpo-umano), and all three cells are 88px tall (equal height). Language toggle Profile it→IT triggers one additional /api/discover-batch?lang=it and Home shows no previous layer. 320x640 Home has no horizontal overflow. 0 console errors during the full run. ONE reproducible issue found: at the first card, a right-drag (rubber-band scenario) navigates to /deep-dive/ instead of elastically snapping back — see rca_of_issue.

ui_bugs.issue: At the first card (cursor=0), a horizontal RIGHT-drag (~150px) intended to trigger the rubber-band navigates to /deep-dive/<id> instead of snapping back. The Pan gesture appears not to cancel the underlying HomeStoryCard tap when translation is blocked (canPrev=false). Left-drag / swipe-left works correctly. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/home-story-deck.tsx:96-110 (Pan.activeOffsetX([-10,10]) + card Pressable onOpen).

issues: Category tile labels wrap to two lines because 4 tiles in a row leave very narrow cells (e.g. 'Technolo\n gy', 'Corpo\n umano'). No horizontal overflow, but tile labels look cramped at the smallest supported width.

action_items: Investigate rubber-band vs tap disambiguation at cursor=0. When Pan gesture is 'blocked' (canPrev=false && translationX>0), ensure the Pressable inside HomeStoryCard cannot fire onOpen for the same interaction. Possible fixes: raise Pan.activeOffsetX to a smaller value (e.g. [-6,6]) so pan claims earlier, wrap the card in a Gesture.Native().requireExternalGestureToFail, or handle onOpen only on Gesture.Tap composed with Pan.
Cosmetic: at 320px, consider reducing category tile columns to 3 or shrinking font/padding so labels stay on one line.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is 1599 lines — still worth splitting into feature routers (media, discover, user, tts, purchases).

home-story-deck.tsx: the tap-on-active card is only guarded by `!moving.current` inside onOpen; a Gesture.Tap composed with the existing Pan (Gesture.Exclusive/Race) would remove the current ambiguity between rubber-band and tap.

story-info-grid uses `boxShadow: `0px 10px 24px ${colors.glassShadow}` as any` — proper cross-platform shadow (shadowOffset/shadowOpacity/elevation) would avoid the `as any` cast and web-only fallback.
seed_data_creation: None. All tests use anonymous user IDs generated per-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend media cache warm-up now runs on startup and logs '710 files' warmed. discover-batch enforces count ≤ 14 (422 on 15) and returns unique ids honouring exclude. Frontend Home renders a strict linear deck (prev=0, next=1 on first render), fires ONE /api/discover-batch initially, prefetches heroes before rendering (Image.prefetch of first COVERS_BEFORE_SHOW=3), and appends new batches with exclude= only when cursor is within PREFETCH_AHEAD=3 of the end. discover-next is not called anywhere in the Home flow. Only outstanding UI issue is rubber-band at first card triggering tap→deep-dive; validate with real touch or after gesture composition fix.
rca_of_issue: Rubber-band bug RCA: HomeStoryDeck wires the pan handler on <View testID='discover-swipe-area'> via GestureDetector with Gesture.Pan().activeOffsetX([-10,10]). Inside the same viewport, each StoryLayer renders HomeStoryCard which is (per usage) a Pressable that calls onOpen. On web, Playwright emits mousedown at (x0=0.15*width, y=0.5*height) followed by 12 tight mousemove steps of ~12.5px each and mouseup. Two of my three trials showed the deck NOT recognising the drag as a Pan (canPrev is false so translation is dampened *0.16 and never crosses the visual threshold; the JS Pressable inside receives mousedown+mouseup within its bounds and fires as a click). Steps to reproduce: open /discover on 390x844, without moving cursor perform mouse.down at ~15% width of discover-swipe-area, drag +150px right over ~50–100ms, release → URL changes to /deep-dive/<active story id>. Expected: card should elastically resist and spring back with URL unchanged. Mitigation: compose Gesture.Race(pan, tap) so pan wins even when translation is dampened, or move onOpen to a Gesture.Tap on the card that requires pan to fail (Gesture.Simultaneous+manualActivation) — see action_items.
